cases.description: A DATA event cannot depend on the output that its own bytes would create.
A peer trigger cannot name an output absent from the normalized timeline.
Cancellation cannot cause a later peer stimulus for the cancelled RPC.
A peer trigger cannot name a caller action outside the action sequence.
An await-output action cannot name an output the expected timeline never produces.
An await-output action cannot gate the peer DATA that would produce the awaited output.
A later caller action cannot complete before an earlier await-native action observes its target.
A streamed request message cannot precede acceptance of the write action that supplied it.
No later peer event can follow trailers, transport close, failed connection, or DATA end-of-stream.
A write cannot be accepted after caller input has half-closed.
Only the first successful half-close can be accepted.
A write after cancellation is rejected locally and cannot become a native request.
The terminal observation is the final semantic timeline event.
connection-outcome requires success.
response-headers requires a nonempty header block.
DATA requires bytes and endStream.
trailers requires a nonempty header block.
transport-close admits no fields from another peer-event variant.
GOAWAY requires the current-RPC acceptance observation.
reflection-response requires version, bytes, and RPC status.
channel-ready admits no unrelated observation fields.
rpc-opened admits no unrelated observation fields.
request-message requires its contiguous index.
input-accepted requires action and accepted-message index.
input-rejected requires its action index.
input-half-closed admits only its optional action index.
output requires an index and lossless JSON value.
final-status requires a gRPC status code.
cancelled requires its cause.
action-failed requires action and cause.
terminal requires disposition and cause.
OpenAPI synthesis remains on revision 5 when gRPC revision 7 is added.
gRPC synthesis accepts only revision 7.
The legacy AsyncAPI synthesis corpus remains on revision 4 in this snapshot.
gRPC processor scenarios cannot occupy AsyncAPI's independently reserved revision 6.
AsyncAPI processor scenarios cannot occupy gRPC's revision 7.
The reflection transcript cannot carry implementation-private fields.
Synthesis reflection starts with list-services on its one stream.
A synthesis reflection transaction does not repeat an identical query.
The returned service inventory and closure-query set cannot omit one another.
Every returned non-infrastructure service receives one closure query.
Duplicate JSON members are rejected before host-parser selection.
Changing a two-output server stream to unary is rejected.
An incomplete end-of-stream frame cannot complete successfully.
A gRPC frame flag outside zero and one is rejected.
Application metadata cannot occupy the grpc- reserved namespace.
Binary metadata is represented as canonical Base64 bytes, not an ASCII value.
Normalized request metadata must retain configured value order.
The normalized final status must equal peer grpc-status.
Duplicate grpc-status values cannot produce one valid final status.
A reflection response version must match the query that triggered it.
A reflection response cannot depend on an absent application output.
Every reflection request host equals the carried authority including its port.
A reflection stream cannot change valid_host after its first response.
A v1alpha fallback retains the v1 transaction deadline rather than refreshing it.
A fallback cannot open after the one discovery deadline has expired.
Every reflection request carries only the configured discovery metadata.
grpc-timeout must be the exact non-shortening encoding of the configured duration.
Native cancellation count must equal normalized cancellation observations.
A limit terminal requires a peer message that exceeds the declared inbound ceiling.
An oversized native request cannot terminate for an unrelated cause.
gzip request configuration requires gzip header and per-message compression evidence.
A compressed response frame without one supported non-identity encoding is a protocol failure.
A caller action can produce only its permitted normalized result kind.
Semantic and native request-message observations have identical cardinality.
Malformed grpc-message remains nonfatal and its exact raw spelling is retained.
A present rich-status code must equal the nonzero final grpc-status.
Malformed Protobuf in grpc-status-details-bin is a protocol failure.
Duplicated grpc-status-details-bin is a protocol failure.
Application metadata cannot occupy the binding-owned te field.
Application metadata cannot occupy the binding-owned user-agent field.
Discovery metadata cannot occupy the binding-owned content-type field.
Discovery metadata cannot occupy the binding-owned user-agent field.
A serverName DNS spelling cannot carry a trailing dot.
serverName carries no port.
An IP serverName is unbracketed.
An IPv6 serverName carries no zone identifier.
An IP reference identity sends no SNI.
A TLS identity override never changes dial or HTTP authority.
Application DATA cannot precede the one initial response-header block.
An RPC has exactly one initial response-header block.
The initial response-header block carries exactly one three-digit :status.
A duplicate :status makes the response-header block invalid.
grpc-message is singular even though a comma remains legal inside its one value.
A decimal status outside zero through sixteen normalizes to UNKNOWN.
Rich-status code comparison uses raw grpc-status before UNKNOWN normalization.
Client-streaming input comes only from indexed writes, never the harness initial-input member.
Only application/grpc and application/grpc+proto establish the revision-one Protobuf response representation.
A post-open limit terminates the native RPC with exactly one cancellation.
A failed connection remains pre-open and preserves security versus transport cause.
Response pseudo-headers precede every regular header.
Native application sends preserve the exact timeline and input order.
A native application send cannot exist without one ordered request-message event.
Native reflection requests preserve version fallback order.
A native reflection request cannot exist without its one ordered discovery query.
Descriptor-driven request conversion is bound to the exact structured invocation value.
Application response headers admit only the :status pseudo-header.
Unknown grpc-reserved response fields are not custom metadata.
grpc-encoding is forbidden in terminal trailers.
HTTP/2 pseudo-headers are forbidden in trailers.
content-type is an initial response field, not a trailer field.
Inbound binary custom metadata uses only standard padded or unpadded Base64 spellings.
Inbound ordinary custom metadata is nonempty printable ASCII.
Inbound binary metadata refuses otherwise-decodable spellings with nonzero unused Base64 bits.
Every normalized leading metadata group is retained in native evidence.
Native response metadata cannot invent a group absent from the controlled peer block.
Normalized response metadata groups remain Unicode-scalar name ordered.
Native binary metadata evidence retains every decoded octet sequence in encounter order.
Lossless request evidence preserves the caller's valid Timestamp offset spelling while conversion uses the same instant.
Lossless request evidence preserves the exact caller floating-point value through descriptor conversion and wire framing.
Any conversion resolves by the final path component while retaining the exact caller type URL.
An impossible civil Timestamp remains a pre-dispatch conversion refusal rather than host-date normalization.
A decoded well-known value outside its companion invariant cannot become an application output.
Normalized metadata names use direct Unicode-scalar ordering, including punctuation, independent of locale.
A negative-zero double remains bit-distinct from positive zero through request conversion.
Float32 conversion applies binary32 underflow before request serialization.
The minimum subnormal input is rounded to the exact binary32 wire value.
The maximum finite float32 spelling is rounded without double-precision leakage.
The empty string is the valid default bytes spelling rather than invalid Base64.
A canonical integer map key is encoded as its exact typed wire key; leading-zero aliases are refused separately.
JSON null maps to google.protobuf.NullValue zero rather than failing enum conversion.
Bool map keys admit exactly lowercase true and false.
Integer map keys reject nonnumeric strings.
Typed map keys enforce the declared signed width.
Typed map keys enforce the declared unsigned width losslessly.
Noncanonical integer map aliases are refused rather than normalized into a typed-key collision.
A nonfinite Value number alternative cannot be silently serialized as JSON null.
Positive infinity in Value number_value fails output conversion.
Negative infinity in Value number_value fails output conversion.
NBSP is not RFC JSON whitespace.
Unicode line separator is not RFC JSON whitespace.
A JSON string value cannot contain an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate.
A JSON member name cannot contain an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate.
Ordinary null is skipped before field assignment when descriptors arrive through JSON FDS.
Ordinary null is skipped before field assignment when descriptors arrive through binary FDS.
Ordinary null conversion is invariant under reflection v1 descriptor carriage.
Ordinary null conversion is invariant under reflection v1alpha fallback carriage.
Processor float conversion rounds to binary32 before deciding finite overflow.
Unsigned map keys reject a negative-zero spelling before dispatch.
Signed-plus and leading-zero integer map-key aliases are refused by the portable caller profile.
An unset google.protobuf.Value alternative is not an output JSON null.
A finite source number that rounds to binary32 infinity is refused.
Any packing refuses a selected ordinary type whose descriptor admits the reserved @type envelope spelling.

Native framing evidence for a valid non-printer-canonical Duration must retain the exact normalized payload length; the runtime gate separately rejects leading-plus input with internally consistent expected bytes.
Any unpacking refuses a selected ordinary type whose descriptor emits the reserved @type envelope spelling.
The @type JSON spelling remains usable when the same message is not packed in Any.
A null original-name occurrence still consumes the field spelling before an alias duplicate.
A corpus JSON document has exactly one value and no trailing token.
Duplicate decoded member names are rejected at every JSON depth.
Every corpus carrier is decoded with fatal UTF-8 before host JSON parsing.
Duplicate outer corpus members cannot be sanitized before conformance evaluation.
A UTF-8 BOM is preserved through fatal decoding and rejected by the RFC JSON lexer.
The portable caller profile refuses a standard-plus and URL-underscore alphabet mixture.
The portable caller profile refuses a URL-minus and standard-slash alphabet mixture.
Null on an ordinary wrapper-valued field leaves it unset and does not select presence.
Null for google.protobuf.Value materializes NullValue and selects its containing oneof.
The portable caller profile refuses quoted numeric enum alternatives after declared and custom names.
An unknown closed-enum singular number remains unknown-field material and absent from typed output.
An unknown closed-enum expanded occurrence is omitted without discarding recognized occurrences.
An unknown closed-enum packed occurrence remains unknown-field material under reflection carriage.
Closed-enum input refuses quoted numeric alternatives across singular, expanded, and packed positions.
Binary string UTF-8 validation recurses through nested, repeated, map and Any message positions before output conversion.
The ordinary own JSON member name __proto__ survives parsing, descriptor matching, maps and Struct conversion without prototype semantics.
Closed-enum typed absence and recognized-value retention compose across expanded, packed, map, and oneof positions.
Proto2 UTF-8 is validated after singular merge so an overwritten invalid occurrence does not poison the surviving string.
Protobuf varints have at most ten octets and the tenth octet is at most one.
The portable caller profile refuses quoted numeric enum spellings even when a broader runtime parser could consume them.
Quoted enum fallback does not accept exponent syntax.
Any type URLs require a nonempty prefix before the final slash.
A smallest-message collision among original and effective JSON spellings excludes every reaching method.
A sibling method whose message closure is collision-free remains invocable.
Edition CLOSED enum output has the same typed-absence boundary as proto2.
The portable caller profile refuses Base64 spellings with nonzero unused pad bits.
When an explicit json_name differs, only it and the original field name are accepted; the default lowerCamel spelling is not a third alias.
An Edition enum accepts an exact-integral JSON number and performs an actual wire round trip instead of treating it as a string-only custom-enum path.
An Edition field with explicit json_name continues to admit its original field spelling, but not an ungoverned default-lower-camel alias.
A terminating tenth value octet is accepted in ordinary scalar and map-key value contexts, while an eleventh-octet value remains malformed.
